newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran disabled veterans protest at German embassy.
newsitem.headline: Iran disabled veterans protest at German embassy.

text.p: Several thousand Iranian veterans disabled in Iraqi chemical attacks held a sit-in outside the German embassy in Tehran on Thursday to protest against a verdict accusing Iran of ordering political killings.

Tehran radio said the protesters, in their second day of demonstrations outside the mission, were also backing demands to bring to justice German firms which allegedly supplied toxic chemicals to Baghdad during the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war.

The demonstrators had marched to the embassy on Wednesday in the fourth demonstration at the barricaded mission after the court accused Iranian leaders of ordering the 1992 killings of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.
Iran has repeatedly denied any role in the slayings, which it blames on infighting between opposition groups.
The radio also carried reports from other protest marches against the verdict which were held on Thursday in half a dozen cities across Iran, including the oil-rich Khuzestan province.
Tehran has said court proceedings would begin shortly against 24 German companies accused of having helped Iraq produce chemical weapons during the war.
The ruling issued last Thursday sparked a diplomatic row between Iran and Germany, until recently Tehran's main trade partner and most important Western friend.
Iran has responded to the recalling for consultations of all European Union ambassadors, except Greece's, by announcing it would reciprocate.
